_meta.what_this_is: A screening scenario: a detector (a classifier, a test, a content filter) with a known sensitivity and specificity, applied to a population where the thing it looks for is RARE. This is the setup for the base-rate fallacy -- the reason a detector everyone would call excellent (99% sensitive, 95% specific) flags mostly false positives when prevalence is low. The numbers are a fixture so the confusion matrix and PPV are exact.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. Round population and rates so TP/FP/TN/FN are whole numbers and checkable. No trained model.
_meta.format: population; prevalence; sensitivity (P(flag|positive)); specificity (P(no flag|negative)); sweep_prevalences for the base-rate sweep
